quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Stop next to the car in front of the parking space.
Back slowly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop next to the car in front of the parking space.
questions.explanation: After you find a parking space and signal, stop parallel to the car in front of your space. Then turn your wheel to park.

questions.question: Is it illegal for a car to share a lane with a motorcycle?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full lane. Two motorcycles can share a lane, but cars cannot share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots before changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: What color are signs for public recreation areas?

options.text: Orange.
Red.
Green.
Brown.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown.
questions.explanation: Brown signs mark public recreation areas and historical sites. They help you find places when you are traveling in new areas.

questions.question: How do you pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions?

options.text: Do not cross the center line.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road, you must use the lane meant for oncoming traffic. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: The signal is about to change to a red X.
Do not drive in this lane.
You can only turn left in this lane.
You can drive normally in this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can drive normally in this lane.
questions.explanation: Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed as traffic flow changes. A green arrow means the lane is open and you can drive normally.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look for traffic, then go if the road is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Slow down and go carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs indicate?

options.text: School zones.
No passing zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones. The sign will have text to confirm it is a no passing zone.

questions.question: How should you treat railroad crossings?

options.text: They are safe because trains rarely come.
They are dangerous.
They are safe places to park.
You must always stop there.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are dangerous.
questions.explanation: Always treat railroad crossings as dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: On a road without sidewalks, where should pedestrians walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side as traffic flow.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing the traffic nearest them.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly and wait for an opening.
Speed up faster than the traffic around you.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the speed of freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic. This helps you merge smoothly and safely. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to look at a map for directions.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: If a car coming toward you has high beams on, where should you look?

options.text: Either side of the road
The center of the road
The right side of the road
The left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the bright lights and helps you stay on your course until the other car passes.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed slowly and with caution. Look both ways before entering.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway angles toward the left. What does this mean?

options.text: An intersection is just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You will need to turn left just ahead.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line marks the edge of the road. When the edge line angles toward the center, the road is narrowing ahead.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.
Follow other cars more closely.
Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery roads. Slow down and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left and you reach an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object in the road.
questions.explanation: A cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid an object. Always be extra careful around bicyclists.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to your previous lane.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane. Always turn into the lane nearest to the direction you came from.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A broken line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator gets stuck open while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Press hard on the brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off the engine. Be careful not to lock the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine. Be careful not to lock the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When the accelerator sticks, the engine keeps the car moving even when you take your foot off the gas. Turn off the engine carefully—just enough to stop it without locking the steering wheel. Then press the brakes and drive to a safe area.

questions.question: Which tip does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that dark window tint makes it harder to see at night.
Keep a flashlight in your car.
Look directly at oncoming headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly at oncoming headlights.
questions.explanation: Looking at bright headlights causes your pupils to shrink. After the car passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to the darker light. During this time, you cannot see well and are essentially driving blind.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before you shift into reverse.
Walk around the back of the car before getting in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors.
Turn up the radio to alert people around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around the back of the car before getting in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because drivers cannot see clearly behind their cars. Always walk to the back of your vehicle first to check for children and small objects before you back up.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you with bright headlights. What should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until they dim theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: When an oncoming car has bright headlights on, look away from the lights and toward the right edge of the road. This keeps you from being blinded while the car passes.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They have large blind spots.
They can stop faster than regular cars.
They need the same amount of space as regular cars.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Avoid staying in these areas. Because of their size and weight, trucks need more room to turn and stop than regular cars.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: Road hazard warning.
Interstate route.
School crossing.
Speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road hazard warning.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped and yellow. In work areas, they may be orange. These signs warn you about hazards ahead or areas where special rules apply.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an intersection with no traffic lights or stop signs?

options.text: Keep your speed and go through.
Stop, look both ways, and then go.
Let all other drivers go first.
Be ready to yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no stop sign or light, you must yield to cars coming from the right. Always be prepared to yield to prevent a crash. Do this by easing off the gas, being ready to brake, and looking left, right, and left again.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway is starting.
Divided highway is ending.
Bumpy road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway is ending.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the divided highway will end ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road is getting wider.
One lane is ending; the right lane will close soon.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.
One lane is ending; the left lane will close soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: One lane is ending; the right lane will close soon.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: Your car has an Anti-Lock Braking System and is losing grip on a slippery road. What should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal down.
Press and hold the gas pedal.
Tap the brakes lightly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal down.
questions.explanation: If your car loses grip on a slippery road, press hard on the brake pedal, keep holding it, and steer away from danger. The ABS system automatically pumps the brakes faster than you can. Lifting your foot or pumping the brakes yourself will turn off the ABS.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road turns sharply right, then left.
The road turns sharply left, then right.
The road curves to the left.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road will turn sharply right and then sharply left.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph may need ____ to stop completely.

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Large trucks take much longer to stop than cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph needs about 400 feet to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Narrow bridge ahead.
A lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.
Industrial area.
Freeway on-ramp ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. This sign warns you that the right lane is ending or the road is getting narrower.

questions.question: Driving faster affects your vision how?

options.text: You can see more area around you.
You can see less area around you.
It is easier to see cross traffic.
It does not change your vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see less area around you.
questions.explanation: When you drive faster, your field of vision becomes smaller. As speed increases, you must be more alert to dangers.

questions.question: What should drivers do when driving in bad weather?

options.text: Drive faster to reach their destination sooner.
Follow other cars more closely.
Stay farther behind other cars.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: In wet weather, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. This gives you more time to stop safely.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.

options.text: White
Blue
Green
Orange

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with black markings. They control traffic and must always be obeyed.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After the turn, your car should be in:

options.text: The right lane.
The center of the street.
The left lane.
The lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should end up in the left lane, which is closest to the lane you came from.

questions.question: At a reduced conflict intersection, you cannot turn left.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Reduced conflict intersections reduce crashes and injuries on divided highways. At these intersections, drivers must turn right first, then make a U-turn if needed.

questions.question: A work zone:

options.text: Can be moving or stationary.
Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require you to slow down.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving (like vehicles striping lines, mowing, or removing snow). They have orange signs with black markings. Always slow down and stay alert in work zones.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow traffic signal, you should:

options.text: Merge in the direction of the arrow.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn left after checking for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Turn left because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left after checking for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. But oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and to pedestrians.
